name: UpsellPlus
summary: Upsells, cross-sells and free gifts across Shopify product pages, cart, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and POS, with AI recommendations and A/B testing in 23 storefront languages.
best_for: shopify merchants who want one app covering product page, cart, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and POS offers rather than three, especially Shopify Plus stores, where the checkout half of the product actually unlocks
skip_if: your upsell revenue sits near the $500 ceiling that Free and the $49 plan share — the first paid step buys features, not headroom — or you are not on Shopify Plus and were buying this for the checkout upsells
honest_knock: The plans are capped by the revenue they are allowed to earn you, and the first paid step does not raise that cap: Free and the $49 Launch plan both stop at $500 of upsell revenue a month. The $49 buys offers and features, not headroom — headroom starts at $119. And crossing a ceiling is not something you decide: their FAQ says you are automatically upgraded to the next tier so the offers keep running, so a good week moves the invoice on its own. Read the feature list closely too, because the tier named Shopify Plus is not the same thing as the requirement — their FAQ says Plus is needed only for checkout customization and checkout upsells, so on a standard Shopify store the checkout half of a checkout-upsell app is not what you are buying. The last thing to know is at the top, and it is not on their pricing page. The plan card says Scale stops at $5,000 a month while the comparison table on that same page says Unlimited; we asked, and UpsellPlus support confirmed on 21 September 2026 that Scale is a revenue ladder - $199 up to $5,000 of upsell revenue a month, $299 up to $10,000, $399 up to $15,000, $499 up to $20,000, $699 up to $30,000, $799 up to $40,000, and an Unlimited plan at $999 with no ceiling - and that passing $5,000 moves a store to the $299 tier on its own. That is better news than the Enterprise tier above it suggests, but it means the number you are quoted at signup is the floor of a ladder whose higher rungs are not published anywhere.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Launch · per month, or $500 a year
pricing.notes: (listing and vendor pricing page re-verified 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/upsellpluscheckout, USD; the Scale ladder confirmed in writing by UpsellPlus support on 2026-09-21) Fixed monthly tiers based on the revenue generated through UpsellPlus offers, with no percentage commission. The listing shows four: Free runs one offer, opens all twelve upsell types plus analytics, and allows up to $500 in upsell revenue. Launch is $49 a month or $500 a year (saves 15%) and allows the same $500 of app-generated revenue a month, adding cart, pop-up and drawer upsells, product page and post-purchase upsells, multivariate A/B testing, progress bars and free gifts. The tier named Shopify Plus is $119 a month or $1,149 a year (save 20%), raises the ceiling to $2,000 a month and adds checkout customization, checkout upsells, thank-you page customization and AI recommendations. Scale is $199 a month or $1,899 a year (save 20%) for up to $5,000 a month, live support and multivariate A/B testing. 14-day free trial on the paid tiers; charges billed every 30 days. The vendor's own page adds two things the listing does not carry: a fifth Enterprise tier with no published price, sold through a demo, and a Managed Service at an extra $499 a month. That page contradicts itself on Scale - the plan card and the listing both say up to $5,000 a month, while its comparison table puts Scale under Unlimited - so we asked the vendor. UpsellPlus support answered on 21 September 2026 that Scale is a ladder rather than a single price: $199 up to $5,000 of upsell revenue a month, $299 up to $10,000, $399 up to $15,000, $499 up to $20,000, $699 up to $30,000, $799 up to $40,000, and an Unlimited plan at $999 with no ceiling. A store that goes past $5,000 is moved automatically to the $299 tier, which covers up to $10,000. So the plan card is the accurate one and the comparison table is wrong, and the amounts above $199 appear nowhere on the published pricing page (figures from UpsellPlus support, 21 September 2026). Hitting a ceiling is not a stop: their FAQ says you automatically upgrade to the next tier so upsells are not interrupted, so the bill rises by itself. Their FAQ also states Shopify Plus is NOT required except for checkout customization and checkout upsells, which is a Shopify restriction; cart, product page, cart drawer, thank-you and post-purchase offers work without it.

compare_with.name: AfterSell
compare_with.why: Both are Shopify upsell apps and both are strongest around the checkout. AfterSell is the tighter, better-known post-purchase and checkout play; UpsellPlus spreads wider — product page, cart drawer, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and Shopify POS in one app, with 23 storefront languages and integrations into Klaviyo, Recharge, Appstle, Skio and Smartrr. The catch is the revenue ceiling on each UpsellPlus tier, so compare on the plan you would actually need rather than on the entry price: free and $49 stop at the same $500 a month.
